summary: Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé was a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Leiden University in 1928 under Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak, whom he succeeded in 1956. Hulsewé taught at Leiden as a Chinese lecturer (1946) and Professor (1956–1975).

Anthony Hendrik Nicolaas Verwey worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Amsterdam and Leiden University, and held a position at the National Museum of Ethnology from 1947 to 1981.
Anthony J. Alston worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Hari Prasad Shastri (circa 1947–1953) and completed his PhD under T. R. V. Murti at Banaras Hindu University (circa 1959–1964).

Anthony Kennedy Warder worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at SOAS under William Stede and doctoral supervisor John Brough. Warder served as Lecturer at the University of Edinburgh (1955–1963) and Department Chairman at the University of Toronto (1963–1990).

Anthony Tribe works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Bristol under Paul Williams and Steven Collins, and earned a DPhil at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. Tribe held posts at the University of Montana and University of Arizona.
Anthony W. Barber works in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1984 and later held an attested post at the University of Calgary in 1998.
Antoine Bazin was a Sinology scholar who studied under Stanislas Julien at the Collège de France from circa 1832 to 1839. In 1852, he served as Secrétaire-adjoint of the Société Asiatique.

Antoine Cabaton worked in linguistics, history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the École du Louvre and École Pratique des Hautes Études under Sylvain Lévi, holding posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, EFEO, INALCO (1907), and École Nationale de la France d'Outre-Mer.

Antoine Grégoire was a linguist and Central Asian scholar. He studied at Liège, Leipzig, Munich, and Paris under Karl Brugmann, Eduard Sievers, Ernst Kuhn, Victor Henry, and Antoine Meillet. He held professorships at Liège (1905–1942) and Université libre de Bruxelles (1936–1945).
Antoine Lutz completed a PhD at Pierre and Marie Curie University under the supervision of Francisco Varela.

Antoine Marie Tabard was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He taught mathematics, physics, and chemistry at St. Joseph's University (1891–1924) and founded The Mythic Society in 1909, serving as its president in 1910.
Antoine Meillet was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Abel Bergaigne and Ferdinand de Saussure.

Antoine Mosac was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He served as Superior of the Jesuit Mission of Chandernagore in 1742 and Superior of the Paris Foreign Missions Society from 1775 to 1777.
Antoine-Gaspard Bellin was an Indologist who earned a Dr.iuris at the University of Lyon (circa 1835–1839). He served as a civil judge and librarian at the Tribunal civil de Lyon.

Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy was a linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He held chairs in Arabic (1795) and Persian (1806) at INALCO, and served as president of the Société Asiatique (1822–1829, 1832–1834).

Antoine-Jean Saint-Martin was a linguistics and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Collège des Quatre-Nations and INALCO under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, later holding posts at the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres, Bibliothèque de l'Arsenal, Imprimerie Nationale, and foreign ministry.
Antoine-Louis Henri de Polier was an Indology scholar who studied under Ramchandra. He served as a Colonel in the East India Company.

Antoine-Léonard Chézy was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Collège de Navarre, Collège de France, and INALCO under Silvestre de Sacy and Langlès. He was Professor of Sanskrit at Collège de France (1815–1832) and Professor of Persian at INALCO (1824–1827).

Anton Boller was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Vienna in 1831. He served as a Dozent and professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at the University of Vienna from 1845 onward.

Anton Eduard Wollheim da Fonseca was an Indologist and linguist. He earned his doctorate at Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp (1828–1831), later lecturing there from 1849 to 1852, and also held a post at the Royal Danish Library.
